newsitem.title: FRANCE: New French mag launched with anti-government slant.
newsitem.headline: New French mag launched with anti-government slant.

text.p: A new French weekly news magazine -- "Marianne" -- was launched on Monday with an anti-government satirical slant and financed independently of any established publishing group, its founders said.

The magazine takes its name from the mythical female figure, Marianne, that adorns France's town halls and some of its currency and which stands for the French Revolution values of "freedom, equality and fraternity".

The new weekly, described by readers as left-wing, was launched in the middle of an election campaign in France, a factor that appeared to be boosting Marianne's sales, the magazine's finance director, Cecile Andre, told Reuters.
She said the new publication was sold out on several newsstands in Paris and in French provinces within a couple of hours of its launch.
"I think readers want another opinion" from those they are getting in other weeklies, Andre said.
France will vote in a two-round snap parliamentary election on May 25 and June 1.
An opinion poll on Monday that was carried out for three mainstream media groups showed the country's centre-right coalition heading for victory by a narrow majority in the elections.

Marianne's founders said the magazine was trying to distinguish itself from France's four other main news magazines by coming out on Monday instead of the usual Thursday and by selling for 10 francs ($1.71) -- half the price of its competitors.

The new publication's main competitors are l'Evenement du Jeudi and Le Nouvel Observateur, described by many readers as politically centre-left, and L'Express and Le Point, described as more right-wing.
The new magazine is the brainchild of Jean-Francois Kahn, a writer and journalist who years ago launched l'Evenement du Jeudi.
Marianne said in an editorial on Monday it aimed to bridge an "appalling gap which has opened up between the people and the world of culture, philosophy, economics and politics".
It said it was the first French journal launched simultaneously on paper and electronically, and directed Internet users to its news in French and English on the World Wide Web.

Finance director Andre told Reuters the advertising response to the new weekly was encouraging, with 4.5 million francs' worth of advertising booked for the first four issues just weeks after Kahn announced the new magazine in February.
The first issue on Monday carried 34 pages of advertising out of 118 pages for a print run of 500,000 copies, but Andre said future issues would have fewer pages.
The magazine, financed independently of any established group by 17 individuals and four finance companies, breaks even with nine pages of advertising and sales of 80,000, she said.

Marianne won approval from France's satirical weekly Le Canard Enchaine, and got conditional praise from Liberation, the daily left-wing newspaper, which also paid for a full-page ad in the first edition.
But readers said Marianne did not have a very different look from its main competitors.
"Finally, is Marianne as different as all that from other weeklies, and notably the Evenement du Jeudi?" asked Liberation. ($ = 5.834 French Francs)
